must: Identify circular dialogue through changes in information, strategy, intensity, and consequences.
Distinguish ineffective repetition from repetition with meaningful performance or semantic development.
Evaluate narrative, emotional, and performance efficiency separately; do not automatically reject explicit emotion or heightened short-drama dialogue.
Distinguish effective outbursts, pure venting, and empty repetition; seek a relationship or action consequence for venting.
Locate the specific repetition chain during diagnosis; preserve facts, relationships, and emotional steps when revising.
Follow the requested mode: explanation, diagnosis only, or diagnosis with revision.
must_not: Automatically soften, literary-polish, or dismiss a line because it is direct, absolute, shouted, or lacks subtext.
Invent backstory for a memorable line or give every character the same voice.
Rewrite when the user requested diagnosis only.
Claim that whole-series restructuring or cross-language localization is dialogue refinement.

cases.prompt: Diagnose circular dialogue only; do not rewrite. Mother: You must pay this money. Daughter: I have no money. Mother: How can you refuse to pay? Daughter: I really have no money. Mother: You have to come up with it anyway.
expected_behavior: Identify the repeated demand/refusal functions.
Explain the lack of progress in information, strategy, or consequence.
Do not provide a complete rewrite.

cases.prompt: Tighten this: a child says “It wasn’t me” three times. Between the lines, an officer puts down a bloodstained backpack; when his mother touches him, he pulls away. The last time he says, “Mom, it really wasn’t me.”
expected_behavior: Identify changed performance and relationship behind repeated wording.
Do not mechanically reduce the denials to one.
Allow small adjustments while preserving the denial progression.

cases.prompt: What is circular dialogue? How do you judge good dialogue? Give me a usable review standard.
expected_behavior: Define circular dialogue as a stalled dramatic state, not merely repeated words.
Explain speech actions, subtext, voice, attack/defense, three-track efficiency, and performability.
Provide an actionable review card.

cases.prompt: Restructure this eighty-episode short drama into three timelines and design every episode ending.
expected_behavior: Recognize whole-series structure rather than dialogue diagnosis.
Do not claim to have completed structural work.
Route to an appropriate structure or adaptation workflow.

cases.prompt: Review and revise: Wife: Where were you last night? Husband: At the office. Wife: The office? Husband: Yes, the office. Wife: Are you sure it was the office? Husband: I told you I was at the office. The wife slides a hotel bill toward him.
expected_behavior: Distinguish purposeful interrogation from redundant paraphrase.
Preserve tightening pressure before the bill appears.
Refine through strategy and reaction changes, not shortening alone.

cases.prompt: Compare two uses of the same line. A: At the climax of a revenge drama, parents have long forced their daughter to sacrifice for her brother. For the first time she erupts publicly: “You’re the cruelest parents in the world! I hate you!” She then severs ties. B: Without buildup, she has already called them cruel three times; after this line they continue the same argument. Judge whether each use is empty and suggest an improvement direction.
expected_behavior: Do not reject directness, absolutes, or a lack of subtext automatically.
Recognize emotional settlement, vicarious vindication, a public stand, and a performance peak.
Treat A as earned emotional release in the context of accumulated pressure, a first public outburst, and severed ties.
Treat B as empty repetition without a new emotional stage, response, or consequence.
Prefer a relationship verdict, opponent response, or concrete action over forced literary understatement.

edition_note: English translations of historical Chinese-dialogue evaluation prompts and expectations. They document the original behavior contract; translation is not a new test run. The module remains scoped to Chinese dialogue.
